llm_proposer.assessment: The most likely cause is a hard WSS input-port failure in the ROADM at S01 at about t=602.5 s. S01 is the only stated element shared by every affected working path, and the simultaneous widespread optical/client failures plus SNCP switching point to a common optical-layer failure rather than a fault local to svc370.

proposals.rationale: A failed WSS input port at the common S01 ROADM can block many channels at once and explains the broad, simultaneous OCH LOS and client failures, including svc370. Some unchanged aggregate optical measurements argue against a total ROADM outage, but are compatible with failure of one WSS input port while unrelated channels remain present.

A switch-fabric failure at the common node could interrupt many ODUs simultaneously. It is less likely because the case contains widespread OCH_LOS and amplifier input-LOS alarms, whereas an OTN switch failure should primarily produce ODU-layer AIS without changing optical signals.

proposals.rationale: A disconnected OMS input could directly cause the AMP_INPUT_LOS on the S01-to-S04 line. It does not by itself explain the simultaneous LOS on S01-to-S15 or the full affected-service set, and upstream amplifier measurements showing no change weaken this alternative.

A severe loss increase immediately before the amplifier in O1 could produce its input LOS. It is unlikely to be the common cause because a single span fault would not explain the simultaneous failure on another S01 outgoing line and the network-wide service pattern.
